subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK questions

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have alignment. High level: ACME is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing summarization + search feature where latency and cost per request are key.

Pain points you shared:
- Current provider has unpredictable latency at peak and high token costs (~3x budget).
- Existing infra struggles with structured outputs and function-calling integration across multiple services.
- Need embeddings for semantic search and a reranking step to improve relevance.

Goals we heard:
1) Reduce per-query cost by ~40% while keeping 95th pct latency under 300ms for short queries.
2) Support deterministic structured outputs to pipe results into ACME’s downstream analytics.
3) Smooth engineering ramp: minimal SDK changes and clear dev docs.

Product fit & integration notes we discussed:
- SDK changes: we recommend using Redwood’s client (node/python) with the streaming API for low-latency token streaming; we can provide a compatibility shim to match your existing call signatures.
- Function calling: Redwood supports function/tool calling; we suggested an early pattern where Redwood returns a structured JSON payload (function response) that your orchestrator consumes.
- Streaming + structured outputs: streaming token events + a final structured JSON payload to guarantee schema.
- Embeddings & reranking: generate embeddings for candidate passages, then use our reranker model (lightweight transformer) to reorder top-K results — we estimate a 12–18% relevance lift based on similar customers.

Action items / owners:
- Marissa (me): share sample integration config & quickstart (attached) and a proposed SLA addendum. Deliver by EOD tomorrow.
- Dev (cc): review SDK shim approach and confirm any blockers on ACME side for function-calling.
- Sarah: confirm internal stakeholders and whether we should loop in your infra/security folks next.

Attachments: redwood-integration-sample-config.yaml (sample client config), redwood-sla-proposal.pdf (draft SLA / pricing appendix)

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Marissa —

Following up on the embedding & SDK notes. A few technical clarifications and recommendations from our side: 

1) Embeddings compatibility
- Redwood’s embeddings are 1536-d float32 by default (similar to many open models). We can return float32 or quantized int8 variants depending on throughput/cost tradeoffs.
- Pinecone compatibility: no schema changes required. We provide a simple batch uploader in the Python SDK (example in the attached sample config).

2) Reranking pattern
- Suggested flow: (a) dense-retrieval to get top-100, (b) run a lightweight reranker (we can host this as a separate route) to score top-10, (c) return top-5 to your app. We’ll include latency estimates in the next doc.

3) Function calling & structured outputs
- We support explicit function schemas; recommend starting with a strict JSON schema for the response object to avoid downstream parsing errors.
- Streaming: we stream partial tokens and a final "complete" event with the structured payload so your orchestrator can start consuming tokens while still guaranteeing a final machine-parseable output.

4) Network / security
- For Private/Dedicated customers we support VPC peering and static egress IPs. For hosted, we offer audit logs and token scoping. I’ll loop in our security teammate if you want SOC 2 artifacts.

Next steps (technical):
- I’ll prototype a small Node example showing streaming + function-calling -> structured output into Pinecone and share by EOD Monday.
- Marissa: can you confirm whether ACME prefers Python or Node for the sample?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
